The wrong pair is (4) Ekach Pyala – Annasaheb Kirloskar.

The chapter says that Ekach Pyala was written by Ram Ganesh Gadkari. Annasaheb Kirloskar wrote the musical play Sangeet Shakuntal, which earned great popularity.

The other three pairs are correct: Raigadala Jevha Jag Yete is by Vasant Kanetkar, Tilak Ani Agarkar is by Vishram Bedekar, and Sashtang Namaskar is by Acharya Atre.

Things that help refresh our minds and give a feeling of happiness are the sources of entertainment — hobbies, games, drama and film, writing and reading, and so on.

Healthy entertainment of excellent quality is essential for the healthy growth of one's personality. It keeps our minds lively and fresh and may also make us feel physically more energetic, so that eventually our efficiency at work improves. Pursuing hobbies and games helps in personality development.

In India many festivals, sports and dance-music were developed as forms of entertainment since ancient times, and varied forms of entertainment are available in the modern period as well. Entertainment can be classified into two categories, active and passive: watching a sports match, listening to music or watching a movie are examples of passive entertainment, in which we are not actual participants but only viewers.

The rulers of the Bhosale family of Tanjore were great patrons of drama; some of them wrote plays and translated Sanskrit plays. The 19th century saw a great development of the Marathi theatre. Vishnudas Bhave is known as the father of the Marathi theatre, and Seetaswayamvar was the first play he presented.

The movement he started was followed by historical, mythological and light farcical plays, the farcical ones dealing with social issues in a humorous way. Initially no written scripts were used — often only the lyrics were written down and the dialogues were spontaneous. V.J. Kirtane was the first author to write a script, Thorale Madhavrao Peshwe, in 1861, and a printed copy was made available; this began the tradition of having a complete written script ready before staging a play.

The growing popularity of classical music, promoted by Balkrishnbuva Ichalkaranjikar and later by Ustad Alladiya Khan, Ustad Abdul Karim Khan and Ustad Rahimatkhan, led to the origin of musical Marathi theatre. Sangeet Shakuntal by Annasaheb Kirloskar became very popular, and Sharada by Govind Ballal Deval commented humorously on the custom of marrying young girls to aged men. Mooknayak by Shripad Krishna Kolahtkar, Sangeet Manapaman by Krishnaji Prabhakar Khadilkar and Ekach Pyala by Ram Ganesh Gadkari are also important.

The early Marathi plays were staged on open grounds; the British first built closed theatres such as Play House, Rippon and Victoria in Mumbai, and the shows gradually moved into them. Later the popular plays of Acharya Atre helped the Marathi theatre through a temporary decline, and recent plays on historical themes such as Raygadala Jevha Jag Yete by Vasant Kanetkar, Ghashiram Kotwal by Vijay Tendulkar and Tilak Ani Agarkar by Vishram Bedekar became very popular.

The students of history can avail of many professional opportunities in the fields of drama and movies.

In drama, deep knowledge of the history of the arts and architecture of the period concerned is essential in order to achieve accuracy of stage backdrops, and experts in these fields can work as art directors or consultants. Script writers and dialogue writers also need the assistance of experts in languages, in the history of languages and in the cultural history of a given period.

In cinema, the art directors of movies create the backdrop designs of atmosphere, costumes and jewellery, make-up and hair styles suitable to the times in which the story is set, and scholars of history can work in this field as art directors or as consultants to the art director. Writing movie dialogues also requires knowledge of the culture and the language as spoken in the period concerned, so experts in these fields can find many professional opportunities.

A film set in the past has to place its audience in that period, and every visible element must belong to it.

The art directors of movies create the backdrop designs of atmosphere, costumes and jewellery, make-up and hair styles, and all of these must be suitable to the times of the theme of the movie. Writing the dialogues needs knowledge of the culture and of the language as it was spoken in the concerned period.

None of this can be done accurately without a study of the history of that period, so scholars of history are needed in the film industry as art directors or as consultants to the art director, and expertise in history is therefore important in it.

A Bharud is a metaphorical song that carries spiritual and ethical lessons, and is comparable in style to a road show.

The Bharuds composed by Saint Eknath are popular in Maharashtra because of their wide range of subjects, their dramatic quality, their easy rhythm and their humour. Saint Eknath composed them with the purpose of educating people on various aspects of life, so they teach while they entertain, and that is why they have remained popular.

The honour of making and releasing the first full length movie goes to Maharashtra, and the chapter therefore calls Maharashtra the land that nurtured the Indian film industry.

The contribution of Madanrao Madhavrao Pitale, of the Patwardhan family of Kalyan and of Harishchandra Sakharam Bhatvadekar, also known as Savedada, was very important in the development of Indian movies. Gopal Ramchandra Torane, also known as Dadasaheb Torane, along with A.P. Karandikar, S.N. Patankar and V.P. Divekar, sought help from foreign technicians and made a movie entitled Pundalik, released in Mumbai in 1912.

Raja Harischandra, directed by Dadasaheb Phalke, was the first movie to be processed completely in India and was released in Mumbai in 1913. He also made the silent movies Mohini-Bhasmasur and Savitri-Satyavana and documentaries on the rock-cut caves of Verul and the pilgrim centres of Nashik and Tryambakeshwar, after which a tradition of making movies on historical and mythological subjects came into being.

Anandrao Painter was the first to make a cine-camera of Indian make. His cousin Baburao Painter, known as 'Mistri', made Sairandhri in 1918 and the first historical movie, Simhgarh, and also historical movies like Kalyancha Khajina, Bajiprabhu Deshapande and Netaji Palkar, as well as Savakari Pash on a realistic social issue. In 1925 Bhalaji Pendharkar made Bajirao-Mastani, which the British government banned as a suspected medium of spreading nationalistic sentiments. Sant Tukaram, in which Vishnupant Pagnis acted as Saint Tukaram, received international acclaim and was shown at the international film festival in Paris. Production studios such as 'Bombay Talkies', 'Rajkamal Productions', 'R.K. Studios' and 'Navketan' played a significant role in the development of the Indian film industry.

Powada (ballad) is a dramatic narration made by alternately reciting poetry and prosaic extracts. It narrates the great deeds of heroic men and women in a very forceful and inspiring style.

Two well-known examples are the Powada composed by Adnyandas, a contemporary poet of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, narrating the incident of the killing of Afzal Khan, and another on the battle of Sinhagad composed by Tulasidas.

In the British period Powadas were composed narrating the stories of Umaji Naik, the Chapekar brothers and Mahatma Gandhi, and during the 'Samyukt Maharashtra' movement the powadas were used as a medium of the movement.
